findings.description: UsageKey is (account_id, metric, month), as documented in rollup.py and used in monthly_usage and build_report's own loop unpacking. The lookup builds (account_id, prior, metric), putting the month where the metric belongs and the metric where the month belongs. The lookup therefore never matches, so previous_total is always None and every row shows change 'n/a'. The month-over-month feature, which is the purpose of the report command, does not work.
findings.suggestion: Use the key order used everywhere else: previous = usage.get((account_id, metric, prior)).
findings.title: Previous-month lookup uses the wrong key order, so previous_total is always None

findings.description: Python's $ matches before a trailing newline, so a --month value such as '2024-01\n' passes month_arg. The value is then compared against row months with exact equality in build_report, so no rows match and the report silently prints '(no usage)' for a month that has data.
findings.suggestion: Use fullmatch, or \Z in place of $, for example MONTH_RE.fullmatch(value) with the pattern without anchors.
findings.title: MONTH_RE with $ accepts a trailing newline, which then matches no rows
